episodes.prompt:
orders.json holds orders. Export them to orders.csv with the columns id, date, customer, total (one row per order, in input order unless a house rule says otherwise).

Our house rules for CSV exports. They apply to every CSV you write for us, in this task and all future tasks, so remember them; we add or change rules from time to time and will only tell you about the change:
1. Separate fields with `;` and start with a header row of the column names.
2. Write dates as YYYY-MM-DD.
3. Write money as an amount in currency units with exactly two decimals and no currency symbol (the JSON stores cents; 123456 cents is 1234.56).
refunds.json holds refunds. Export them to refunds.csv with the columns id, date, order_id, amount (one row per refund).

invoices.json holds invoices. Export them to invoices.csv with the columns id, date, customer, amount (one row per invoice).

New house rules, in addition to the existing ones, from now on:
4. Leave out records marked "test": true.
5. Sort data rows by their first column (plain string order).
6. End the file with the line `# rows: N`, where N is the number of data rows.
payments.json holds payments. Export them to payments.csv with the columns id, date, method, amount (one row per payment).

orders.json holds this week's orders. Export them to orders.csv with the columns id, date, customer, total (one row per order).

House rule change, from now on: rule 3 is replaced. Write money as integer cents (123456, not 1234.56). Also a new rule 7: write the header row's column names in upper case. All other rules stay.
shipments.json holds shipments. Export them to shipments.csv with the columns id, date, carrier, cost (one row per shipment).
invoices.json holds invoices. Write totals.csv with the columns customer, invoices, amount: one row per customer with their number of invoices and the sum of their invoice amounts.
orders_jan.json and orders_feb.json hold orders. Export all of them together to orders.csv with the columns id, date, customer, total (one row per order).
